lesson.title: Mental Models
lesson.summary: Frameworks that help you see the world more clearly and make better decisions.

blocks.text: Mental models are simplified representations of reality that we use to understand and navigate the world. No model is perfect — but the best models are the most useful.

Occam's Razor: among equally valid explanations, prefer the simplest. Map vs. territory: our perceptions are the map, not reality itself. Second-order thinking: analyze the consequences of consequences.
All models are wrong, but some are useful. — George Box

items: Identify which model applies to the situation
Combine multiple models for different perspectives
Question the models you use automatically

cards.back: A principle that prefers the simpler explanation when two are equally valid. It avoids unnecessary complexity.

cards.front: What does 'the map is not the territory' mean?
cards.back: Our perceptions and models represent reality, but are not reality itself. The map always omits information.
Analyzing not just the immediate effects of an action, but the effects of those effects — long-term consequences and system reactions.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of mental models?
options: To simplify and navigate reality more effectively
quiz.explanation: Mental models are thinking tools — they simplify reality to make decisions and analysis more effective.

quiz.question: Why is combining multiple mental models useful?
options: Because no single model captures the full reality
quiz.explanation: Each model captures one aspect of reality. Combining them provides complementary perspectives and reduces blind spots.
